domain_restrictions: r is between 0 and n inclusive.
Therefore n is a nonnegative integer.
The index m in the q-factorial definition is a nonnegative integer.
q is treated as a formal indeterminate, not as a quantified variable.
The equality is intended as an identity of polynomials in q.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every pair of integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient defined by the stated q-factorial formula satisfies the symmetry [n choose r]_q equals [n choose n-r]_q, viewed as a polynomial identity in q.
quantifier_order: For all integers n and r, assuming 0 <= r <= n.

variables.name: m
variables.role: auxiliary index in the product definition

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are present in the statement.
The value of the q-binomial coefficient is determined directly from n, r, and q by the given formula.

statement_nl: For all integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, if the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient is defined by [n choose r]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}), where (q;q)_m := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^i) and (q;q)_0 := 1, then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q as polynomials in q.
